title: Move the Factory and its embedded payload to the ticfac CLI
description:
Move the Factory to the ticfac CLI.

First, a correction to the Phase 2 scope. jrj says to move this "without hidden
tk dispatch shims", implying they exist. THEY DO NOT. A survey found no
exec.Command("tk", ...), no os.Executable, and no re-entry into the cobra tree
anywhere in internal/factory. The one place that touches tk's command surface
runs the OTHER way: internal/factory/tkcommands.go regex-scans the embedded
shell entrypoints for `tk <sub>` invocations and asks a caller-supplied
`has(chain []string) bool` whether this binary implements them. The cobra lookup
lives in the caller in cmd/tk. That is a gate, not a shim. Do not go hunting.

What moves: ~7745 non-test lines over 24 files, five packages —
internal/factory (5290: deploy, credential setup, status, supervisor read,
rollout, migration, wrangler/docker drivers, bundle staging),
internal/factory/dashboard (1502, a read-only TUI over runs and gates),
internal/factory/credentials (232, reads/writes ~/.ticfacrc), plus three doc.go
contract-parity homes.

Commands: `tk factory deploy|setup|status|dashboard` (cmd/tk/cmd/factory.go:57,
133, 212; factory_dashboard.go:74) and the thin slice `tk cloud
run|stop|status|logs|trace|supervisor` uses (LoadCredentials, ReadSupervisor,
Supervisor*, SecretGatewayBaseURL, RunWorkflowName).

In Go terms it is near-standalone: no import of internal/tick, tickboard or
tkcontract from production code. THE REAL COST IS THE EMBEDDED PAYLOAD. //go:embed
cannot reach across modules, so moving internal/factory means moving
cloud/factory and cloud/sandbox and the module-root embedded.go with it;
cloud/sandbox alone is 236K of build context. Then the required-tk-commands gate
needs a way to interrogate a tk it no longer ships beside.

Touchpoints are few: `~/.tick/factory/bundle` as a staging dir (deploy.go:142),
one `git remote get-url origin` (setup.go:1406), docker (toolchain.go:59,124)
and wrangler (wrangler.go:206). No herdr references at all. It never reads or
writes a tracker record.

This tick is INDEPENDENT of the herdr executor work and can run in parallel with
it. If it grows past one tick, split it rather than widening it — say so in the
RESULT file and propose the split.
acceptance_criteria: factory, its dashboard and its credentials build and pass under ticfac with their embedded payload; the factory and cloud commands work from the ticfac CLI; the required-tk-commands gate still verifies the entrypoints against a tk it no longer ships beside, and the RESULT file says how; ticks no longer carries the factory tree; no ticks Go package is imported; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green.
